examples.title: Ethanol combustion, balanced
examples.description: Ethanol burning in oxygen, balanced by the exact balancer (nullspace of the atom matrix): C2H6O + 3 O2 → 2 CO2 + 3 H2O.

examples.title: Industrial processes in the library
examples.description: The reaction library filtered to the industrial class (Haber–Bosch, the contact process, N2O4): open one in the builder, the mechanism viewer or the energy profile from here.

examples.title: SN2 mechanism: bromoethane + hydroxide
examples.description: Bimolecular substitution in one concerted step with back-side attack and inversion; step through it in the mechanism viewer.

examples.title: SN1 mechanism: tert-butyl bromide hydrolysis
examples.description: Unimolecular substitution: the slow ionisation to a tertiary carbocation, then capture by water. Four states with the energy of each.

examples.title: Fischer esterification mechanism
examples.description: Acid-catalysed ester formation from acetic acid and ethanol in six states: protonation, addition, proton transfer and loss of water, all reversible.

examples.title: Diels–Alder: cyclopentadiene + maleic anhydride
examples.description: A concerted [4+2] cycloaddition giving the endo adduct: six electrons move in one cyclic transition state.

examples.title: Aldol addition mechanism
examples.description: Base-catalysed addition of ethanal to itself: enolate formation, attack on a second carbonyl and protonation of the alkoxide to 3-hydroxybutanal.

examples.file: 08 Hydrogenation of ethene - catalysed or not.kreact
examples.title: Hydrogenation of ethene: catalysed or not
examples.description: The energy profile of C2H4 + H2 → C2H6 with and without a metal catalyst (Pd, Pt, Ni): the catalyst opens a path with a far lower barrier and leaves ΔH unchanged.

examples.title: Haber–Bosch equilibrium (Kp)
examples.description: N2 + 3 H2 ⇌ 2 NH3 at 400 °C (673 K) with Kp = 1.6e-4 atm⁻² from 50 atm N2 and 150 atm H2: the ICE table gives the partial pressures at equilibrium and the conversion.

examples.title: N2O4 ⇌ 2 NO2 and Le Chatelier
examples.description: The brown/colourless gas equilibrium N2O4 ⇌ 2 NO2 (Kc = 0.0059 at 298 K, ΔH = +57 kJ/mol) with the Le Chatelier panel ready: add N2O4, halve the volume or heat to 350 K and press Apply.

examples.file: 11 Consecutive reactions A to B to C.kreact
examples.title: Consecutive reactions A → B → C
examples.description: Two first-order steps in a row (k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2): the intermediate B rises, peaks and falls while C appears after an induction period.

examples.title: Michaelis–Menten enzyme kinetics
examples.description: E + S ⇌ ES → E + P with k1 = 10, k−1 = 1, kcat = 2 and [E]0 = 0.01: the initial velocities at six substrate concentrations follow the hyperbola v = Vmax·S / (KM + S), and the Lineweaver–Burk plot recovers KM and Vmax.

examples.title: Brusselator oscillator
examples.description: A model chemical oscillator: with B > 1 + A² (here 3 > 2) the concentrations of X and Y settle onto a limit cycle and oscillate for ever.

examples.title: Reaction order from data
examples.description: Concentration against time for an unknown reaction (synthetic, with scatter): the order analysis fits zero, first and second order and picks the straight line, which is second order here.

examples.title: Arrhenius plot: activation energy
examples.description: Rate constants measured from 300 to 380 K (synthetic, with 1 % scatter): ln k against 1/T is a straight line whose slope gives the activation energy and whose intercept gives the pre-exponential factor.
